title: Former Olympic sprinter Adam Gemili working with Chelsea academy
content:
British sprinter Adam Gemili has revealed he is working with Chelsea’s academy youngsters after announcing his retirement from athletics on Monday.

Gemili, a former 200m European champion and world championship gold medallist in the 4×100, relay, has called time on a 15-year sprinting career in which he raced against Usain Bolt, Justin Gatlin, Yohan Blake and Noah Lyles, and also battled numerous injuries.

Chelsea sources confirmed to The Athletic that the 32-year-old, who spent seven years as a promising young footballer in the club’s vaunted academy before switching to athletics, has been welcomed back to Cobham on a casual basis to work within the player care team.

“I’m just a normal guy from Dartford, we didn’t grow up with a lot,” Gemili told journalists. “We just worked hard and I committed to my sport.

“I just hope one or two of (the academy players) take some inspiration from that and say ‘you know what, it doesn’t matter if I can’t do it in this way, I’ll always find a way to be successful’.

“It doesn’t matter what you do. My story is my own and I hope a lot of these guys can create their own stories.

“I really hope they will go on and become super famous, rich, successful footballers that I can ring up and say ‘oh, I need some tickets for this game’, but the reality is it might not happen.

“But they might then be able to go: ‘Adam used to do that and then he became a professional athlete in another sport, maybe I can do that’.”

Gemili also announced that he plans to set up his own academy to help young athletes from a variety of sports improve their speed.

“Knowledge is power and if I’m able to teach these kids everything that I know, I can die happy,” he added.

“I hope even just one or two of them can feel some sort of inspiration from my story because football is very tough sport — like, I never planned to become an athlete.

“For a lot of these guys they won’t make it to the top level, they won’t make it to the top of the Premier League.

“But if I can teach them the skills that I got, one or two of them might even come into athletics, you never you never really know.”
